a.headline: UK startup snares $20m to recreate gigs with hyper-realistic digital avatars
a.summary: Unit1 has secured major investment to produce AI-powered digital versions of musicians for live concert experiences, positioning itself as a lower-cost alternative to shows like Abba Voyage. For motion and visual communication students, this raises urgent questions about synthetic performance, visual identity, and what constitutes authentic creative presence.

a.headline: Affinity 3.3 shows that Canva is serious about taking on Adobe
a.summary: The latest Affinity update signals that Canva is making a calculated push into professional design software territory, challenging Adobe's long-held dominance in the creative tools market. As a student, understanding this shifting software landscape matters for your future practice and the economic structures shaping which tools studios adopt.

b.headline: Former EPA officials: Trump is letting data centers make people sick
b.summary: Former Environmental Protection Agency officials are warning that deregulation is allowing AI data centres to emit pollutants that directly harm communities living nearby, with health impacts being ignored in the race to build AI infrastructure. This piece connects the physical cost of your generative tools to real environmental injustice, a conversation every design student using AI platforms should be part of.

b.headline: South Africa joins the global resistance against American data centers
b.summary: Civil rights organisations in South Africa are mounting coordinated protests against the expansion of US-owned AI data centres on the continent, raising questions about digital colonialism and resource extraction. This international perspective is vital for design students thinking about where AI infrastructure is built and who bears the environmental and social cost.

b.headline: AI slowdown calls justified but collapse of bubble may be more immediate threat
b.summary: Analysis from The Guardian examines the scale of debt being used to fund rapid data centre construction for AI, questioning whether the economic model underpinning generative AI tools is sustainable. For design students, understanding the fragile financial architecture behind the AI boom matters when evaluating which tools and platforms to build your practice around.

c.headline: Ester Pazur on being a pessimist, the power of stop-motion and why handmade art still matters
c.summary: After losing commissions directly to AI, stop-motion animator Ester Pazur began sharing her hand-drawn work online and found a growing community of practitioners who value slow, material-based making as a deliberate stance against automated image production. This is an honest and grounded account of what it means to keep a handmade practice alive in a market being reshaped by generative tools.

c.headline: Marina Willer crafts letters with light and projection for BFI London Film Festival's new identity and campaign
c.summary: Pentagram partner Marina Willer has built the new BFI London Film Festival identity around analogue light projection and physical letterforms, consciously choosing process-led craft in an era dominated by digital shortcuts. The work is a clear statement about slowness and materiality as design values, and a compelling counterpoint to the AI-generated visual branding flooding the industry.
